doc.title: Ray Bryant interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: 'Little Susie' and its success
summary: The tune evolved with the Jo Jones trio and was a hit when recorded in 1959-60.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Going back to, you were talking about “Little Susie,” did you have a sense when you recorded that tune that, you know I think this tune’s really going to do well for us? Or does it sometimes come as a real surprise that one particular thing hits and the others don’t?

Well I wasn’t surprised at this because we had tried it out on so many audiences before making the record. I mean actually I recorded it with the Jo Jones trio when I was with Jo. It hadn’t really evolved to what it ended up being like when I did it under my own name in 1960, or the last part of ‘59. But having played it in so many clubs and joints around, and seeing the reaction of the people to this tune, I knew that if we ever got a chance to put it down on a record, the way that it had evolved to be, it would probably do very well. And that’s the way it turned out.
